The Maple Leafs ended a nine-game winless streak that featured eight regulation losses with a 4-2 victory against the New York Islanders at UBS Arena. It was their first win since Halloween. "Everyone's done it," McKenna said with a smile when asked if he's nervous about the bill he's about to pay, "so I'm all good." McKenna and the Maple Leafs finally earned some credit by how they played against the Islanders, finding some confidence and momentum for the first time in a long time. items.body: Forward gets assist in loss to Kings after trade from Red Wings Dylan Larkin made his Montreal Canadiens debut Monday in a 2-1 loss to the Los Angeles Kings and the capacity crowd at Bell Centre crowed about its coup. items.summary: Kaprizov scored four points in Minnesota’s 5-2 win in San Jose on Monday.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Bob Frid-Imagn Images Minnesota Wild star Kirill Kaprizov set a new team scoring record on Monday with a point in his 15th consecutive game. Kaprizov, 29, was named the first star of Monday’s game against the San Jose Sharks after scoring a goal and three assists en route to a 5-2 Wild victory. Across his past 15 games, Kaprizov has collected eight goals and 29 points. The 5’10” winger now ranks second in NHL scoring with 49 points (19 goals, 30 assists) through 26 games this season. Kaprizov previously set the Wild franchise record with a 14-game point streak back in the 2022-23 season. Additionally, he is now on a six-game multi-assist streak, trailing only Wayne Gretzky for the longest such streak in NHL history . Four different Wild players scored goals in their 5-2 win in San Jose on Monday, with Joel Eriksson Ek tallying twice and Kaprizov, Blake Coleman, and Brock Faber each scoring once. With their victory, the Wild remain atop the NHL standings with an 18-3-5 record and 41 points through 26 games this season. They remained dominant in San Jose despite missing Quinn Hughes, who sustained an injury in a game against the Calgary Flames last week. The Wild originally selected Kaprizov in the fifth round (No. 135 overall) of the 2015 NHL Draft. After a successful KHL career with three different teams, most notably CSKA Moscow, Kaprizov joined the Wild in the 2020-21 season and immediately established himself as a star player. In 423 career NHL games across seven seasons with the Wild, Kaprizov has collected 249 goals and 524 points. The Novokuznetsk, Russia product has added 19 goals and 36 points in 36 playoff contests. items.title: Flames’ Morgan Frost exits game with upper-body injury
items.summary: Frost was hit hard by Ottawa’s Tyler Kleven early in the second period on Monday.
items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Calgary Flames center Morgan Frost left Monday’s game against the Ottawa Senators during the second period after sustaining an upper-body injury. Frost, 27, was visibly shaken up after taking a hard hit from Senators defenseman Tyler Kleven early in the middle frame. After heading down the tunnel toward the Flames’ dressing room, Frost briefly returned and played a couple more shifts before leaving the game for good. Kleven was not penalized for the hit, but Flames winger Joel Farabee was assessed two roughing penalties for his role in the post-whistle scrum; Ottawa’s Ridly Greig was also called for roughing on the play. Frost logged 8:53 of ice time, took one shot on goal, and finished with a minus-one rating across 10 shifts before exiting Monday’s game. The Flames ultimately lost the game by a 2-1 final score. Through 25 games with the Flames this season, Frost has collected five goals and 14 points. The Aurora, Ont. product is under contract with the Flames at a $4.375 million contract through the end of 2026-27, at which point he can become an unrestricted free agent. The Flames acquired Frost and Farabee together from the Philadelphia Flyers midway through the 2024-25 season. Frost set a new career high with 22 goals in 82 games with the Flames in 2025-26; he tied Mikael Backlund for second on the team with 43 points. The Flyers originally selected Frost in the first round (No. 27 overall) of the 2017 NHL Draft. The 6’0″ center followed up a strong junior career with the OHL’s Soo Greyhounds by turning pro within the Flyers organization in 2019-20, appearing in his first 20 NHL games with the club that year. In 417 career NHL games over parts of eight seasons split between the Flyers and Flames, Frost has collected 80 goals and 204 points.

items.summary: Dylan Larkin’s first night as a Canadien gave him plenty to look forward to, as he left the rink “excited about the future” despite a loss to the Kings.
items.body: MONTREAL — Leave it to the Los Angeles Kings to get in the way. They live to suck excitement out of a game and the energy out of a building, and they succeeded in doing that Monday. This was Kings hockey at its awful best, employing the antithesis of entertainment—a 1-3-1 system that ideally would’ve been retired when Jacques Lemaire stepped off the New Jersey Devils’ bench for the last time in 2011—to slow-burn their way to a 2-1 win over the Montreal Canadiens . The Kings were in the way in the neutral zone for 59 minutes of this game before getting in the way of five consecutive Canadiens shot attempts in the final minute of play. Down four-on-six, Los Angeles defenceman Brian Dumoulin dove to the ice and blocked Dylan Larkin ’s shot at a wide-open net and, in the process, blocked the one story everyone suffering through that painfully boring and seemingly endless game was hoping for—a dramatic tying goal from the newest member of the Canadiens. At least the Kings didn’t steal away Larkin’s excitement on what he termed “a very emotional night.” The 30-year-old’s first game as a Canadien came after what had to have felt like the longest 26 days of his life as a Red Wing, and he’d lived through miserable ones through 10 playoff-less campaigns over his 11 years in Detroit. Larkin spent these last days away from the franchise that drafted him 15th overall in 2014, holding out for a trade after 824 games with that winged wheel on his chest, watching as the hole in his wallet grew bigger and bigger with each passing day of his team-imposed suspension. And then everything changed dramatically with one phone call. items.title: McKenna’s clutch winner helps Maple Leafs end skid
items.summary: Fitting that the teenager with boundless confidence was the one to deliver for a veteran group that was slowly losing theirs.
items.body: ELMONT, N.Y. — Leave it to the lightest guy on the team to hoist the heaviest monkey off their back. When Gavin McKenna busted to the New York Islanders’ crease, pounced on a juicy rebound and finally scored on a penalty call that felt as delayed as a Toronto Maple Leafs victory, the teenager delivered a fist pump 23 days in the making. A punctuation mark on the third-period winning goal of a 4-2 comeback and First Star performance by an 18-year-old prodigy who can’t recall the last time he’s ever been on any hockey team that has lost nine in a row. “Just a big relief,” McKenna said. “That was a huge win for us. Obviously, a big monkey off the back for everyone. Hopefully, we can carry that momentum and hopefully get hot here.” The thermostat had been gradually cranked to nursing-home levels in Leafland since the slumping club’s last victory, which was on Halloween in Vancouver. Fitting that the teenager with boundless confidence was the one to deliver for a veteran group that was slowly losing theirs. “He’s played in a lot of high-pressure games,” said Chris Tanev , who tied the game with his first snipe since April 2025. “I’m sure since he’s six years old, he's been the best player on best teams playing in the best tournaments around the world. And, I mean, he's a first-overall pick for a reason, because I'm sure he usually shines in those moments. So, I mean, it's huge for him to get us a goal and get us a win.” Funny enough, McKenna had missed a similar look one period earlier, when Matthew Kessel’s extended skate got just enough rubber to deflect the puck clear of Ilya Sorokin’s half-vacant net. items.body: Bylsma discusses why teams having trouble protecting late leads The Coaches Room is a regular feature throughout the 2026-27 season by former NHL coaches and assistants who turn their critical gaze to the game and explain it through the lens of a teacher. In this edition, Dan Bylsma, former coach of the Pittsburgh Penguins, Buffalo Sabres and Seattle Kraken and assistant with the New York Islanders and Detroit Red Wings, examines some of the reasons behind teams struggling to protect multigoal leads and defending against 6-on-5. So far this season, comebacks and 6-on-5 goal-scoring are more prevalent. These are two things that go together: Teams have come back from two or three goals down and, often, scored 6-on-5 to do it. The Winnipeg Jets came back after trailing by four goals twice in a span of 12 days. The Florida Panthers were the only team in NHL history to do that previously, accomplishing it twice (Nov. 12-21, 2019, and April 2-5, 2022). Winnipeg scored a 6-on-5 goal and a 6-on-4 goal in overcoming a 4-0 deficit in a 5-4 overtime win against the Montreal Canadiens on Nov. 3 and came back from 4-0 down again, with help from another 6-on-5 goal, in a 5-4 shootout victory against the Chicago Blackhawks on Nov. 14. The Dallas Stars came back from two goals down in the last 1:18, scoring twice 6-on-5 before defeating the Vegas Golden Knights 4-3 in overtime on Nov. 17. items.body: Linus Ullmark continued his impressive start to the season on Monday, making 34 saves to lead the Ottawa Senators to a 2-1 victory over the Calgary Flames. Michael Amadio and Shane Pinto each scored, allowing Ottawa (16-6-3) to close out its three-game homestand with a 2-0-1 record. Matt Coronato scored the lone goal for the Flames (10-13-2), who were playing the first of a five-game Eastern road trip. Devin Cooley, who continues to look for his first road win of the season (0-4-0) was busy, stopping 29 of 31 shots. The Flames made it a one-goal game, 2-1, when Coronato scored a third-period power-play goal beating Ullmark glove side. The Flames found themselves short-handed early in the second after Ottawa’s Tyler Kleven caught Morgan Frost with a hard bodycheck that sent the Calgary forward to the ice. The hit was reviewed but no penalty was assessed. Joel Farabee was instead handed a double minor for roughing after coming to Frost’s defence, while Ottawa’s Ridly Greig received a roughing minor. With 48 seconds remaining in the period the Senators had a scare when Tim Stutzle hit the goalpost and grabbed his left knee. The Senators leading scorer went right to the dressing room but was back on the ice for the third. Amadio opened the scoring midway through the period when he intercepted the puck out front, made a move to pull Cooley and beat him glove side. Just over five minutes later Pinto stepped into the faceoff circle and snapped a shot past Cooley for his 10th of the season. Cooley faced a flurry of shots in the early parts of the period and made four straight saves to keep the Senators at bay. With Monday’s win the Senators matched their longest point streak, nine games (7-0-2), since a run in 2014-15.

items.title: Blackhawks’ Bedard out four months after undergoing shoulder surgery
items.body: Connor Bedard will not be returning to the ice until early spring. Bedard will be out for four months after undergoing successful shoulder surgery, the Chicago Blackhawks announced on Monday. Bedard got hurt on a face-off early in the third period against the Toronto Maple Leafs last Tuesday. The 21-year-old centre slammed his stick on the ice and held his right arm in front of him as he made his way to the locker room. Blackhawks general manager Kyle Davidson told reporters Saturday that Bedard would undergo right shoulder surgery after exiting that win over the Maple Leafs. Chicago placed Bedard on the injured reserve Sunday and recalled forward Dominic Toninato in a corresponding move. Bedard has a history of shoulder issues. He missed extended time last season with a right shoulder injury and underwent surgery on his left shoulder during the off-season. Bedard missed the Blackhawks' first five games of the season rehabilitating that injury. The 2023-24 Rookie of the Year, Bedard had 18 points (seven goals, 11 assists) in 15 games since returning. He became the second-youngest captain in Blackhawks franchise history at the start of the season. Chicago is last in the Central Division with an 8-14-2 record and now faces even more of an uphill climb without their star player for most of the season.

To thin out the forward corps, the Red Wings have placed Sheldon Dries on waivers, per Sportsnet’s Elliotte Friedman . Dries, 32, has already spent more time with Detroit than he expected this year. After spending most of his first two years in the Red Wings organization with the Grand Rapids Griffins in the AHL, Dries inked a two-year, $1.75MM extension with Detroit last February. Primarily an injury replacement, Dries went scoreless in five games for the Red Wings last season. He was exceptional in the AHL, registering 23 goals and 45 points in 57 games with a +20 rating. Unlike last season, Dries has played for the Red Wings more often than not. Since Detroit suspended Larkin without pay, Dries has held down a consistent role in the Red Wings’ lineup. Still, he hasn’t been that productive, registering only one assist in 16 games while averaging 10:06 of ice time per game. In his brief time with the Griffins this season, Dries has scored five goals and eight points in games with a +4 rating. Still, although he hasn’t been as offensively fruitful as he has been in the AHL, Dries has found other ways to contribute. Before being placed on waivers, Dries was fifth on the team in hits (34), and he has held his own defensively, maintaining a 90.7% on-ice SV%, good for 11th on the team.

The defenseman was being further evaluated after he left a 4-1 win at the Calgary Flames on Thursday following a hit from Flames forward Adam Klapka at 9:57 of the third period. Wild coach John Hynes did not have an update after the game and declined to specify the nature of the injury prior to a 4-3 shootout loss at the Vancouver Canucks on Saturday, but a concussion has been ruled out. “He's not going to play on the trip, so he's going to go back to Minny and get reevaluated now and we’ll have some more info,” Hynes said before the game. Hughes has 21 points (six goals, 15 assists) during a NHL career high 13 -game point streak (including a goal and an assist Thursday) that set a Wild record for defensemen. Hughes ranks second among NHL defensemen with 34 points (eight goals, 26 assists) in 24 games. items.body: St. Louis Blues centre Robert Thomas , Dallas Stars goaltender Jake Oettinger and Chicago Blackhawks defenceman Sam Rinzel have been named the NHL's three stars of the week. Thomas led the NHL with 10 points (two goals, eight assists) and a plus-11 rating in four games as the Blues climbed into the final wild-card position in the Western Conference with a perfect week. The 27-year-old became the first St. Louis player since Keith Tkachuk in 2005 to record three straight three-point games. Oettinger went 3-0-0 with a 1.94 goals-against average, .933 save percentage and one shutout as the Stars extended their winning streak to five games and moved into second place in the Central Division. His 33-save performance in a 1-0 win over Pittsburgh on Sunday marked his league-leading fifth shutout of the season and the 21st of his career. Rinzel led all NHL defencemen with eight points (1-7) in four contests to power the Blackhawks to a 3-1-0 week, capped by his first career overtime goal against Calgary last Saturday.

We have a wonderful opportunity ahead of us in a great hockey city, and I’m excited to help build something new and meaningful for the community. I’m proud to be a part of it and look forward to what we can accomplish together.” Jenner is one of the most decorated players of her generation. Forward Kiefer Sherwood has been moved to injured reserve, retroactive to his last game on November 15th. That will make him eligible to return as soon as he’s healed up from an upper-body injury that has him out week-to-week . With the roster spot vacated by Sherwood, San Jose has also recalled defenseman Libor Hajek . Hajek will join Michael Kesselring as extra defenders in the Sharks’ lineup. Of the two, it could be the left-handed Hajek who stands a better chance at working into the lineup. Nolan Allan has recorded just four points in 11 games this season while operating on San Jose’s bottom-pair. While he scored in the Sharks’ last outing, that production might not be enough to keep him in the lineup in a matchup against a Wild team without superstar Quinn Hughes . Kesselring hasn’t done much to command minutes either, with four points and a minus-eight in 24 games this season. Those struggles could open the door for Hajek to play in his first NHL game since the 2022-23 season. He appeared with the New York Rangers that year, notching one goal in 16 NHL appearances and six points in 24 AHL games. Hajek moved to the AHL’s Wilkes-Barre/Scranton Penguins for the first half of the 2023-24 season, then opted to move to the Czech Extraliga from 2024 until 2026. He won a league championship with Pardubice HC in 2026, after combining for 32 points in 111 games over three seasons with the club. items.body: Register Login Flames Recall Sam Morton By Gabriel Foley | at November 23, 2026 11:07 am The Calgary Flames have recalled forward Sam Morton from the AHL’s Calgary Wranglers. He will provide extra depth after Martin Pospisil was injured in Saturday’s loss to the Chicago Blackhawks. Calgary seemed prepared for Morton’s recall, with the centerman being held out of the Wranglers’ Sunday matchup. Morton will now receive his first call-up of the season, and his first since signing a one-year extension with Calgary over the summer. The 27 year old has scored six points, eight penalty minutes, and a minus-three in 20 games with the Wranglers this season. He has been a go-to depth forward through the last two seasons – though that role has only resulted in Morton making four NHL appearances. He’s marked those games with one goal and 10 penalty minutes. Morton has otherwise been productive in the minor-league. He reached a career-high 45 points in 70 games of the 2024-25 season, good for the fifth-most points on the Wranglers that season. He repeated that standing last season, notching 38 points in 68 games to rank fifth again. The Flames will have Morton as an option for Monday’s matchup against the Ottawa Senators. They will decide between Morton and Brennan Othmann to fill the hole left open by Pospisil. Othmann has yet to score through seven games this season. He notched two points in as many games with Calgary last season, after joining the team via trade ahead of the 2026 Trade Deadline. Monday’s matchup could represent another chance to help Othmann find his groove. If not, Calgary will have the gritty Morton to help replace Pospisil’s physical presence.

items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: IMAGN IMAGES via Reuters Connect We can’t say we weren’t expecting big news out of Detroit, but the Red Wings and Montreal Canadiens managed to surprise us nonetheless with a true in-division blockbuster that could change the landscape of the Eastern Conference. The Habs ended a years-long search for a second high-end center, Dylan Larkin, to pair with captain Nick Suzuki. The Red Wings, meanwhile, shipped out the signature player of their long, frustrating wilderness years in exchange for a package that could kickstart a new era of success. Larkin asked out of Detroit in June, shortly after the end of the Wings’ 10th consecutive season without playoff hockey. The American centerman’s full trade protection and the Red Wings’ bizarre willingness to go without a GM for most of the offseason made a clean break unlikely. Still, when Larkin left the team after 10 awkward games with the captain’s ‘C’ stripped from his jersey, his eventual departure became a formality. The question was how Horcoff could get fair value for a very good player and his very reasonable contract; reports suggested Larkin would only waive his veto power to go to a contending team in America. Turns out, at least one team could lure him north of the border. Larkin is off to aid Les Habitants in their quest for Stanley Cup No. 25, as Kirby Dach, Sam Montembeault, the rights to top prospect Michael Hage, and a pile of draft picks go the other direction in Horcoff’s first major trade at the helm of an embattled Detroit club. Did Horcoff get enough to justify trading a top player to a division rival? And is Larkin good enough to elevate the young, hungry Habs from a playoff team to a Stanley Cup favorite? items.summary: The Canadiens and GM Kent Hughes pulled off the practically impossible, acquiring Dylan Larkin to fill a burning hole on their roster. Eric Engels explains why Montreal was right to pay the price in Sunday’s trade with the Red Wings.
items.body: Let that sink in for a second before we get into what general manager Kent Hughes gave up to make it happen. Because getting a second-line centre is an extremely difficult endeavour in this league, but getting one who’s been a first-line centre for the last 11 seasons is practically impossible and Hughes has officially pulled it off here. It took Larkin asking out of Detroit and putting Montreal on the list of cities he was willing to accept a trade to for the opportunity to arise, and it took major negotiating from Hughes with Red Wings interim GM Shawn Horcoff to get the price down from “prohibitive,” as league sources labelled it weeks ago , to acceptable. One Western Conference executive we touched base with right after the trade was consummated late Sunday night praised Montreal's GM, saying, “You only get a couple of cracks at this.” The Canadiens bought themselves at least four cracks at it—and probably five—by shipping out A-level prospect Michael Hage as the headliner on their side of the deal to acquire Larkin, who’s signed through the end of the 2030-31 season for just $8.7 million per year. It could be at least five if/when Canadiens first-line centre Nick Suzuki extends beyond 2030, when his current $7.875-million cap hit is set to expire. But for now, with both Suzuki and Larkin making under $9 million per season, and with the rest of the Canadiens core locked in under $9.5 million per through 2031, a very hard decision became easier to make for Hughes. He came in at the onset of a rebuild in 2022 with hopes of quickly turning the Canadiens into perennial Stanley Cup contenders, and after four years of methodically getting them to the precipice, he had a chance to push them over the edge with one swift move and took it. When the Detroit Red Wings visited the Montreal Canadiens on Oct. 10, the fans at Bell Centre recruited Dylan Larkin.
“WE WANT LARKIN!” they chanted. “WE WANT LARKIN!”
Well, they got him.

For Detroit, the deal finalizes an ugly divorce and bolsters the future. It’s one of the best … It’s, in my opinion, the best atmosphere in hockey, and they’re knowledgeable, and they love their team.” Larkin asked the Red Wings for a trade after last season while using the no-trade clause in his contract to restrict their options. items.body: Register Login Blue Jackets Reassign Steven Lorentz By Brennan McClain | at November 22, 2026 5:31 pm According to a team announcement , the Columbus Blue Jackets have assigned forward Steven Lorentz to the Cleveland Monsters in the AHL. The move allows the Blue Jackets to activate injured winger Conor Garland whenever he recovers from his upper-body injury. Although he wasn’t supposed to be, Lorentz was included in the return package to the Blue Jackets in the Kirill Marchenko trade. Because the Toronto Maple Leafs signed Marchenko to an extension as part of the trade, they had to square that with the 2027-28 salary cap. Since Lorentz is on a $1.35MM salary through the 2027-28 campaign, Columbus accepted him back to facilitate the deal. It was clear relatively early that Columbus didn’t plan to have Lorentz on the roster. After clearing waivers a few days before the trade, the Blue Jackets cut Lorentz from their opening-night roster, and he began the season in Cleveland. Lorentz played really well with the Monsters. Through the first month of the regular season, Lorentz scored seven goals and nine points in nine games with a +2 rating, until the Blue Jackets recalled him on November 5th. Since his call-up, the 30-year-old forward has gone scoreless in seven games while averaging 8:04 of ice time per game. Even if Garland isn’t ready to go quite yet, the clock was ticking on Lorentz’s waiver eligibility. If he had played three more games, or spent 13 more days on Columbus’ active roster, Lorentz would have required waivers again for another demotion. Because they reassigned him today, the Blue Jackets will pause that clock for now.

The Toronto Maple Leafs reached a new low point on Saturday night, blowing a late-game lead to lose their ninth straight game in a 4-3 defeat at the hands of the Columbus Blue Jackets . According to George Richards of Florida Hockey Now , the Panthers are expected to activate captain Aleksander Barkov from the long-term injured reserve on Wednesday. Additionally, veteran winger Brad Marchand will likely return on Wednesday also. Even if only Barkov returns on Wednesday, he alone would make a significant difference in Florida’s outlook. The fact that they could return both Barkov and Marchand is a different story entirely. The Panthers haven’t had Barkov since the first day of October, and haven’t had Marchand since October 6th. Hopefully, for Barkov’s sake, he can maintain some semblance of health for the foreseeable future. After the Panthers repeated as Stanley Cup champions in 2025, Barkov damaged his ACL and MCL leading up to the 2025-26 campaign. Some hoped Barkov could return before the end of the season or the playoffs, but neither happened. Barkov was at the top of a long list of injuries Florida suffered last season, and they didn’t qualify for the postseason. Unfortunately, in his second game back from missing the prior season, Barkov suffered another knee injury. Still, Barkov avoided surgery and was able to rehabilitate, which came with a six-to-eight-week recovery timeline. items.body: David Kirouac-Imagn Images David Kirouac-Imagn Images Could The NHL Learn Something From The PWHL's New Rules? Courtney Nielson Partner Nov 22, 2026 10:03 PM Published Nov 22, 2026 10:03 PM Looking at some of the new PWHL rules coming to this season, could the NHL learn something from those regulations? As the PWHL continues to grow, entering its first season with 12 teams, the league is also developing into its own with unique rules, experimenting with the overtime format, adjusting the high-sticking call, and solidifying bodychecking regulations. The NHL has been criticized season after season when it comes to rules. With the PWHL pre-season around the corner and just over a quarter of the NHL season having passed, could the NHL learn something from the PWHL? Here are some rules that differentiate from the PWHL and NHL. More Videos Choice Of Overtime Penalty Shot Or Power Play (Pre-Season Experiment) Entering the fourth season in league history, all 12 pre-season scrimmages will end with a mandatory five-minute, 3-on-3 overtime, followed by a shootout, regardless of the final score in regulation. Strictly just applying to the pre-season to get a feel for it, when a minor penalty is called in overtime, the non-offending team can choose to take a penalty shot instead of the normal 4-on-3 power play. If the decision is to take the penalty shot, any eligible player in the lineup can take it. Overtime is five minutes and also differs from the NHL in the shootout, where the PWHL uses the best-of-five method versus the best-of-three in the NHL. items.body: Add to Preferred Sources Credit: Marc DesRosiers-Imagn The Chicago Blackhawks announced on Sunday that they have successfully claimed veteran forward Luke Glendening off waivers from the New York Rangers . The move comes at a time when the Blackhawks are desperate for hep down the middle with captain and first-line center Connor Bedard sidelined with an injury to the same shoulder he had surgery on over the summer. The addition of Glendening adds a major element of familiarity for head coach Jeff Blashill, who coached Glendening for a long time with the Detroit Red Wings , as their tenures in the Motor City overlapped from the 2015-16 season through 2020-21. Glendening spent the first eight years of his career with the Red Wings before embarking on several shorter stints throughout the league, including runs with the Dallas Stars , Tampa Bay Lightning , New Jersey Devils , Philadelphia Flyers and Rangers. In four games with the Blueshirts this season, the 37-year-old native of Grand Rapids, Michigan has gone pointless while posting a minus-2 rating in a limited role that has seen him garner an average of 6:15 of time on ice per game. At this juncture of his career, Glendening is likely capped out as a fourth-line option, where has largely played throughout his 938 career NHL games. On Chicago’s roster, that would mean he could draw in on a line that currently consists of Andrew Mangiapane, Ryan Greene and Dillon Boucher.
